headline: NVDA's FY2025 Item 1A keeps the same broad risk map, but it sharpens where execution can fail: longer lead times and component uncertainty are now fused directly into the supply-demand mismatch risk [ev_02], product-transition risk is framed around a more explicit annual Data Center cadence and a disclosed Blackwell yield hit [ev_04], and regulatory exposure is stated more directly around export restrictions and tariffs [ev_09][ev_10].
summary: In FY2024, the supply narrative centered on demand-estimation errors, a broader and faster Data Center launch cadence, and expectations that next-generation products could be supply-constrained even as Hopper supply improved [ev_01][ev_03][ev_05]. In FY2025, NVDA rewrites that section to emphasize long manufacturing lead times and uncertain component availability [ev_02], continued prepaids and new suppliers with added inventory-risk from supply-chain complexity [ev_06], an explicit annualized product cadence with Blackwell-related low yields hurting Q2 FY2025 gross margin [ev_04], and customer ability to invest in AI infrastructure as a named demand variable [ev_07]. On regulation, FY2025 explicitly calls out export restrictions on NVIDIA products and tariffs, whereas FY2024 used broader political and regulatory wording and more transitional China language [ev_08][ev_09][ev_10][ev_11].
card_takeaway: Honest control lane on the same tagged substrate, but it remains ad hoc and visibly noncanonical even after deterministic recovery.
why_this_lane_matters: This is the control because it uses the same tagged substrate as the primary read without the structured contract, making baseline gains visible without pretending B0 is canonical.
